new_findings.title: Retention MaxDeletionsPerRun is checked only before deletion and does not bound concurrent eligibility growth
new_findings.trigger: Initial eligible count is at or below the configured cap, then another application write makes more rows eligible while the batched pass runs. The deletion loop keeps querying and draining until empty.
new_findings.impact: A pass can physically delete more rows than the advertised per-run safety cap and report Deleted greater than Scanned; this weakens the tripwire during concurrent writes. No real data-loss incident is asserted.
new_findings.root_cause: The cap is applied to one initial count. Each delete receives full BatchSize and total is accumulated without checking remaining cap; advisory locks exclude peer retention passes but not domain writers.
new_findings.test_gap: Existing guard tests cover initial count exceeding cap and normal drained batches only. Suggested deterministic regression: MaxDeletionsPerRun=10, initial count=10, delete delegate yields 10, 1, 0. Existing loop returns Deleted=11; then verify a provider scenario with a separate writer before batch2. Neither new regression nor provider scenario executed here.
new_findings.suggested_remediation: Retention owner should define the per-pass cap precisely, bound each deletion by remaining budget and stop/report safely when exhausted; preserve dry-run, cancellation, tripwire and advisory release. Do not apply against working databases.
new_findings.reachability_limit: The loop behavior is statically confirmed; a normal application path that adds past-cutoff eligible rows during the same pass was not demonstrated. Most reviewed policies capture one fixed cutoff and normal newly-completed/deleted rows have current timestamps, so they do not automatically enter that set. Backfill/restore or other concurrent state transitions require separate provider reproduction before claiming normal-runtime impact.
